events.title: The September Massacres of Paris
events.shortBlurb: Revolutionary mobs stormed the Paris prisons and slaughtered priests and religious who had refused the oath against the Church…
body: In the first days of September 1792, as the French Revolution turned to terror and foreign armies advanced on Paris, crowds broke into the city's crowded prisons and killed those held within. Among the first to die, on 2 September, were the priests and religious detained at the former Carmelite convent in the Rue de Vaugirard, cut down for refusing to swear the Civil Constitution of the Clergy that would have separated them from Rome.

The killings spread through the prisons over several days and claimed well over a thousand lives, of whom hundreds were clergy. One hundred and ninety-one of these churchmen — bishops, priests, and religious — were later recognized as martyrs and beatified by Pope Pius XI in 1926. Their deaths mark one of the bloodiest episodes of the Revolution's assault on the Church in France.
